Subject: Dedicated capacity renewal & SLA exception request

Hi Alex / John —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our renewal conversations, Nimbus is looking to:
- Renew the current Dedicated pool for 12 months
- Add an additional reserved pool of 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (mixed availability in Q2)
- Increase committed throughput to guarantee 120 tokens/sec sustained for peak routes

You mentioned procurement would also ask for an SLA exception around latency SLOs and uptime credits tied to the expanded pool. I attached a draft capacity proposal (nimbus_capacity_proposal_v3.pdf) and an internal SLA-exception guidance doc.

Can you confirm the list of endpoints that need the throughput guarantee and whether the exception is timeboxed to the renewal term only? If procurement prefers, we can provide an amendment that explicitly lists the increased reserved capacity and the adjusted SLOs/credits.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm endpoints & procurement points of contact
2) We produce an amendment + formal SLA exception form for legal
3) We schedule a short technical Q/A with Rishi for capacity pairing and rollout timing (15–20 min)

Thanks — happy to get this on a DocuSign once we align.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Marissa —

Thanks for the proposal. Procurement looped me in and asked for two specific items before they can sign:
1) A submitted SLA-exception request outlining the new latency targets (we already have the base SLA but need the exception documented for the additional pool).
2) Quantified uptime credit schedule if Redwood misses the revised SLOs for the expanded capacity.

For endpoints, we need the guarantee on: /api/v1/generate (primary) and /api/v1/embeddings (secondary). Peak windows are 9am–11am PST and 3pm–4pm PST.

Can you also confirm whether the reserved pool will be isolated (no bursting to shared capacity) and the lead time for bringing the GPUs online? Procurement prefers a 4-week lead time from amendment execution.

I attached an internal procurement checklist — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity renewal & SLA exception request (tech input)

Marissa / Aisha —

Thanks for the ping. Quick technical read:
- 8x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs is reasonable for a sustained 120 tokens/sec across the two endpoints if requests are sharded and we enable continuous batching + KV prefix caching for /api/v1/generate.
- Latency SLO recommendations (p95 / p99) for the two routes at sustained throughput: 
  - /api/v1/generate: p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 480ms
  - /api/v1/embeddings: p95 <= 130ms, p99 <= 290ms
- If Nimbus wants tighter p99 targets we recommend enabling int8 quantization for the model variants on the reserved pool — this reduces tail latency but requires a quick model validation pass (1–2 days).
- Uptime credit schedule (suggested timeboxed exception for renewal year):
  - If monthly uptime < 99.9% on the reserved pool for the listed endpoints: 10% monthly credit on that month’s reserved capacity fee
  - If monthly uptime < 99.5%: 25% credit
  - If monthly uptime < 99.0%: 50% credit + remediation plan required

Operational notes: we can tag the pool with a routing policy so production traffic for your account is pinned. Lead time: procurement’s 4-week window is fine — we should start provisioning 3 weeks post-amendment and complete by week 4.

I attached a short SE note (internal) with the quantization checklist and rollout steps. Happy to join the call with Alex and Procurement if you want me on the loop.

—Rishi
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: se_quantization_checklist.pdf
